closest_priors.overlap: Identifies a Hunt–Crossley contact model and learns task-specific nonlinear impedance online, with experimental force–position cost improvement and an inner-loop realization treatment.
closest_priors.residual_delta: It addresses scalar, task-specific identified-contact impedance rather than coupled normal–tangential impedance decisions for continuous scanning across held-out material, geometry, sliding, and history shifts; it also lacks the candidate's explicit wrench, interaction-energy, contact-loss or slip, matched-baseline, and real-time joint evaluation.

closest_priors.overlap: Plans Cartesian stiffness and damping online under tracking and gain constraints and demonstrates real-time operation.
closest_priors.residual_delta: It omits force/torque sensing, soft-contact mechanics, sliding/contact-history shifts, and a force–motion–contact-failure objective with wrench and interaction-energy constraints, so its online gain intervention is not decision-equivalent to the proposed soft-scanning problem.

closest_priors.overlap: Uses a finite-area, velocity-dependent normal–tangential soft-contact model in nonlinear MPC for ultrasound scanning and evaluates tracking on compliant targets.
closest_priors.residual_delta: Impedance is predefined rather than selected online, calibration is narrow, and the work does not pose held-out shift generalization or joint optimality over force, motion, contact failure, energy, and real-time constraints.

closest_priors.overlap: Embeds local Hertz deformation, pressure, and sliding friction in constrained whole-body MPC for compliant contact tracking.
closest_priors.residual_delta: The material model is pre-estimated and impedance remains predefined; it does not study online normal–tangential gain selection across uncalibrated shifts or the candidate's failure-inclusive constrained comparison.

closest_priors.overlap: Provides 6-DoF admittance and wrench regulation for ultrasound-like contact and exposes stability and passivity risks of ideal time-varying impedance.
closest_priors.residual_delta: It supplies an important feasibility boundary but no online impedance-selection objective or held-out optimality study, and therefore does not answer the candidate's decision problem.

closest_priors.overlap: Uses Gaussian-process uncertainty to tighten force-MPC constraints, with simulated contact preservation and sub-10-ms hardware execution.
closest_priors.residual_delta: Its uncertainty is confined to a static output map and it does not update or select coupled impedance gains for moving soft contact across material, geometry, sliding, and history shifts.

search_coverage.summary: The bound Field Map reports sufficient coverage from 49 query events, 99 verified reads, 82 decision-grade cards, and a completed 19-paper active subset with no declared coverage gaps. The supplied evidence spans the nearest online/adaptive impedance, contact-aware MPC, six-axis admittance, uncertainty-constrained MPC, transient/viscoelastic contact modeling, and history-dependent friction families. No supplied decision-grade prior is causally equivalent to the full problem intervention and evaluation scope.

novelty_assessment.residual_unresolved_delta: The surviving problem-level delta is to determine whether online selection of coupled normal–tangential impedance can improve a joint force-regulation, trajectory-tracking, and contact-loss or slip objective while enforcing wrench and interaction-energy limits in continuous soft scanning across held-out material, geometry, sliding-condition, and contact-history shifts, under matched sensing, data, compute, inner-loop, safety, and baseline budgets. The reviewed priors establish separate primitives or feasibility boundaries but do not jointly pose or resolve this decision problem.
